segments.text: Thanks for joining, everyone. Today we're reviewing the new onboarding flow, and I'd like us to decide what ships in the first release.
I'll walk through the prototype first, and then we can dig into feedback. It's a four step flow instead of the current seven.
Step one is account basics, step two is connecting a data source, step three is inviting teammates, and step four is picking a template.
That's a big reduction. Which steps did you remove?
Mostly the profile questions. We were asking for job title, company size, and industry up front, and I moved those to after the first success.
That lines up with what we saw in research. In our last round, five of eight participants hesitated at the company size question.
Did anyone say why?
A few said they weren't sure how it would be used, and a couple said it felt like a sales form instead of a product.
Right, so I'm trying to make the first few minutes feel like getting value, not filling out paperwork.
From an engineering view, removing those fields makes our life easier. Fewer validations and fewer edge cases.
Good. Let's talk about step two, connecting a data source. That seems like the highest friction moment.
It is. In testing, three participants stalled there for more than two minutes, because they didn't have credentials handy.
I designed a sample data option for that. If you don't have credentials, you can explore with demo data first.
That's something I need to look at. How realistic should the demo data be?
Realistic enough to show the product's value. Maybe a hundred sample records with a few charts already built.
I love that idea, but I'm worried about scope. Can we ship it in this release?
I think so. I can reuse the fixtures we built for testing. It's about three days of work, including the toggle to clear demo data later.
Great, then let's include it. Grace, can you own that?
Yes, I'll take it. I'll aim to have it in the staging build by November third.
Perfect. Now, step three, inviting teammates. I added a skip option because research showed people don't always want to invite anyone immediately.
That matches what we heard. Several participants said they wanted to try it alone first.
But from a growth view, invites are our best loop. If we make skipping too easy, we lose that.
That's a fair concern. What if skipping is allowed, but we bring back a gentle prompt after the first successful result?
I could live with that. Let's test whether the later prompt works better than the early one.
I can set up a quick test with six users. If we recruit this week, I can have findings by November sixth.
That would be really useful. Thanks, Omar.
One question on the template picker. Are the templates static, or will they be personalized?
Static for now. We have six templates, and I'd like to rank them by the use case people choose earlier.
That's fine, but we don't capture the use case anymore if we cut the profile questions.
Good catch. I think we need one lightweight question, what are you trying to do, with four choices, before step two.
I'd support that. It's a goal question, not a demographic question, and people tend to answer those more willingly.
Okay, agreed. Elena, can you add that to the prototype?
Yes, I'll update the prototype this week and share it with the team by Wednesday.
While we're on it, accessibility. I noticed the progress indicator relies only on color to show the current step.
You're right, I missed that. I'll add numbers and labels so it works for color blind users and screen readers.
Please make sure that's included in the Wednesday update.
Will do.
Quick thing on copy. Several participants misread the word workspace as a file folder. Can we try project instead?
Interesting. I'll test both labels in the next round with Omar.
Good. Let's talk timing. If Grace builds the demo data, and Elena updates the prototype, can engineering start the flow next week?
Yes, as long as I have the final designs by Wednesday. Then I'd estimate two weeks to build and one week to polish.
That puts us at a release in late November. I'll update the roadmap and let leadership know the timeline.
I'll also write a short summary of the research findings so we have them in one place for the team.
Great. Any last thoughts before we wrap?
Just thank you all. This feedback made the flow so much stronger.
Thanks, everyone. Great session.

action_items.task: Build demo data option and clear toggle for staging
Run six person test on early versus late teammate invite prompt
Update prototype with goal question and accessible progress indicator
Update the roadmap and tell leadership the late November timeline
Write a short summary of research findings for the team

clips.title: Why we cut the profile questions from onboarding
